_comment: Vendored-platform patches for dsh-vscode.
vendor/ is COMMITTED, so these patches normally ride along with it. They are
stored here because vendor/ is also regenerated wholesale on every platform
upgrade (npm install into a staging dir, then robocopy over vendor/node_modules),
which would silently drop them and reintroduce the bugs they fix.
Run `.smoke/platform-patches.py verify` after refreshing vendor/, and `apply`
to put them back. pack.py runs verify before packaging, so an unpatched tree
cannot be shipped. ExpectedPackageVersion guards against applying a patch to a
different upstream release: apply refuses unless the installed version matches.
BASELINE: re-derived against @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.2 (the branch point
was 0.1.5-rc.2). Two 0.1.5 patches were DROPPED because 0.2.2 fixed them
upstream and re-porting would be redundant: dsh-subprocess-local
launchWindowsJob now passes windowsHide: true (lib/index.js:788), and
dsh-win32-process now sets STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW + SW_HIDE on both STARTUPINFOW
sites (lib/index.js:459-461, :627-629). The model-capability UI edit that was
never captured here is also dropped: 0.2.2 natively ships image-input and
reasoning-efforts editors (ModelRow.tsx:172-183). One patch was RETIRED with
no port: dsh-session-persistence-jsonl inspect(id) — its only consumer
(the @dsh-undo bundles) is no longer in the tree (removed in 9a7bf80c),
archive reads go through @mlgbnb/dsh-archive-manager's own log reader, and
better-sidebar uses open(id,'read'), so nothing calls inspect. The package is
now byte-identical to clean 0.2.2 and its guard test is deleted. See
NOTES-0.2.2.md.

why: The released-v0 validators are exact and the v0->v1 migration refuses a
Session carrying anything outside the released shape. Correct for the
released format, but this deployment bakes third-party plugins that wrote
into sessions freely, and one offending event makes a whole session
unobservable. On a real 30-session history the strict validators refused
1251 events across 21 sessions, in four shapes:
1. a content block with a plugin annotation (dsh-file-review's
`dshFileReview` on an empty text block appended to a tool result);
2. a kind:'plugin' source with an extra member (dsh-web-review's
`snapshotId`);
3. a kind:'plugin' source pairing `summary` with a non-notice form
(dsh-mnemon's `instructions` + summary);
4. `subagent/descriptor` version 2 from the `sidechat` plugin, where the
released spec froze on version 3.
0.2.2 FIXED (4) UPSTREAM: subagentDescriptorValue now accepts descriptor
versions 1/2/3 (SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSIONS, lib/index.js:1288-1293)
and assertReleasedEventPayload (:1608-1612) refuses only unknown versions,
so the local v2->v3 coercion is GONE. Shapes (1)(2)(3) are still exact-
refused by 0.2.2 (:650-687 contentBlockValue, :917-948 pluginSourceValue),
so this patch keeps only those tolerances: it drops their unreleased
members and the stray summary, each logged once. Required members, missing
members and unknown kinds still refuse, and the source v0 artifact is never
modified. Verified by a probe importing the real module (annotation,
snapshotId and non-notice summary tolerated; missing members, role/block
mismatch and descriptor version 9 still refuse).
Restores the embedded 'open configuration file' bridge, which 0.1.5 deleted
along with dsh-host-apiproxy.
In 0.1.1 that package's settings handler ran `if (DSH_EMBEDDED === "1")`
and wrote `[dsh-vscode:open-settings] <path>` on stdout so the containing VS
Code extension could reveal the document in its own editor, because the
native opener is invisible in an embedded deployment. 0.1.5 moved settings
to dsh-api-settings-controller, which calls openTextFile UNCONDITIONALLY —
the env check and the sentinel are gone, and openSettingsDocument (unlike
openAgentPresetDirectory) has no 'return the path instead' branch. Nothing
in 0.1.5 reads DSH_EMBEDDED at all (the only DSH_* env seams left are
DSH_AGENTS_HOME, DSH_BUNDLED_SKILL_DIR, DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED,
DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER and DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER), so there is no official
seam to use instead: the panel's 'open configuration file' silently did
nothing after the upgrade.
The patch re-adds the branch in the handler that took over the same job, and
leaves the internals.openTextFile seam intact (asserted by
.smoke/embedded-open-settings-test.mjs, which drives the real controller
with stubbed internals both with and without DSH_EMBEDDED=1). 0.2.2 still
calls openTextFile unconditionally (openSettingsDocument, lib/index.js:443-461,
spawns no DSH_EMBEDDED check), so the branch is ported unchanged into the
same spot (patched lib/index.js:454-467).
Forked child must not inherit the parent's unclaimed pending inbox.
0.2.2 FIXED THE CUT UPSTREAM: latestCompletedPrefixBoundary
(lib/index.js:686-695, lib/types/commands.js:79-90) starts at the last
turn/end and stops before the next turn/start, user/message surface-append
or agent/inbox/spliced, then buildForkSeed (@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/fork)
slices the exact prefix — so the old local `while (cut < ...) type !== turn/
start' loop and its user/message + inbox/spliced additions are GONE from both
files.
What 0.2.2 did NOT fix: the seed is still a verbatim event prefix, so an
agent/inbox/spliced written BEFORE the fork boundary's turn/end still
rehydrates the parent's next-turn/next-step inbox into the child (the child
claims that stale prompt on the user's first send and queues the real new
message behind it). Ported the remaining part only: capture the handle from
this.ctx.agents.create(...) and call handle.agent.inbox.clear() immediately
after it (lib/index.js:848-870 in the patched file).
lib/types/commands.js carries the same ONE-LINE port for the duplicate fork
implementation.
Duplicate fork implementation; same ONE-LINE inbox-clear port as
lib/index.js (the cut loop itself is upstream-fixed in 0.2.2 — see the
lib/index.js entry for the exact anchors).
The one-time windows-acl capability probe spawns the confinement runner around
`cmd /c exit 0` with a bare { timeout, stdio: "ignore" } - no windowsHide - so
that probe can flash a console window on the first host start, exactly like the
per-command spawns did. Same omission, same fix: windowsHide: true. Found by
diffing our patch set against the dsh-silent-pwsh plugin, which patches this
site too; our earlier per-file audit missed it because the file already mentions
windowsHide elsewhere (the bwrap probe), which is precisely the trap the
explore.27 note warns about.
0.2.2 still omits it: dsh-sandbox-local/lib/index.js defaultProbeWindowsAcl
(:157-176) spawns with { timeout, stdio: 'ignore' } only. Ported unchanged.
Global clipboard-write fallback for the embedded VS Code webview.
The webview is a vscode-webview:// iframe embedding http://127.0.0.1:*.
That cross-origin context is denied the async Clipboard API by
permissions-policy, so navigator.clipboard.writeText rejects with
NotAllowedError and every copy button (message copy, mnemon ID copy, ...)
failed silently. The old local patch also replaced the async API with a
synchronous document.execCommand('copy') textarea route, because
execCommand must run inside the user gesture.
0.2.2 did NOT fix this for plugins: its own bundles now carry a private
copy helper (try clipboard.writeText, then execCommand) but that covers
only first-party buttons. Bundled third-party clients still call
navigator.clipboard.writeText directly (dsh-mnemon lib/client.js:6179,
dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces lib/client.js:1270/2909), so the SPA-wide
override is still required. Ported verbatim into the shipped SPA entry.
Verified by fetching GET / from a booted host and asserting the shim is in
the served HTML (boot-test/extension-proxy coverage).
The host CANNOT START inside VS Code without this patch. dsh-app-boot reaches
Node's internal module loader through `node-addon-require-builtin`, whose
native addon identifies the embedder by fingerprint and accepts only an exact
allowlist of Electron builds (0.2.2: 43.0.0, 44.0.0, 44.7.0, 45.0.0-alpha.6).
The extension runs the host on VS Code's own binary as Node
(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1), which is Electron 43.8.3 on VS Code 1.144.1 -- not
on that list -- so the addon answers `Unsupported/no-context` and the host
dies during preparation:
dsh: host preparation failed: node-addon-require-builtin unsupported:
Unsupported/no-context (unsupported Electron runtime fingerprint:
and every boot exits 1, leaving the panel on the error page.
WHY THIS SHAPE. The rest of the platform (cordis-plugin-loader's
requireInternal, dsh-hmr's copy) already resolves internals the same way:
`--expose-internals` first, builtin addon only as a fallback. app-boot was the
one place that hardcoded the addon. The extension always launches the host
with --expose-internals, so the native path is available; verified under
VS Code's binary that require('internal/modules/esm/loader') plus
cjs/loader, helpers, esm/utils and esm/resolve all resolve and expose the
same interfaces the addon returned (resolveSync, Module._resolveFilename,
getCjsConditions, getDefaultConditions, defaultResolve, modern loader).
The fallback keeps a plain node.exe path unchanged, and when BOTH fail the
error names both causes instead of an opaque addon status.
Verified by booting the real host on VS Code's Code.exe (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1,
--expose-internals): the web profile boots, the shell serves, all 14 bundled
entries mount, 7 presets compose; the same command without the patch fails
with the addon error above. Guarded by `boot-test.mjs --electron` and the byte
check in platform-patches.py (pack.py refuses to package a tree without it).
Re-apply after a vendor rebuild: python .smoke/patch-app-boot-internals.py apply
